assessments.reasoning: The exact project overview describes a human-oriented configuration notation and an unambiguous map to a hash table. Its example contains named tables. The project v1.0.0 specification independently reacquired for the identity challenge governs implicit table declarations, redefinition and document-order targeting of declarations. The native publisher bytes matched SHA-256 96096d12cd22ddd1d1eacbf81a48f091545e146d83f6e37931272a00b06fd2f1 and all cited byte ranges.

challenge.method: Test the bare-serialization interpretation against the exact TOML 1.0.0 Keys, Table, Inline Table and Array of Tables sections, and compare native table syntax with the pinned Cargo and audit specimens. Search the frozen canonical entity registry for matching names and IDs.
challenge.results: Dotted keys can create and define intermediate tables. A later header cannot redefine such a table, while it may define a new subtable. An array-of-tables header creates the next table, and nested headers target the last declared element. These native declaration and scope rules identify the notation under Language Index policy even though the project also calls it a format. Package and audit key effects stem from applications. The frozen entity registry contains no matching name or proposed ID.

limitations: The overview capture is explicitly distinct from the supporting v1.0.0 specification, whose exact digest also matches the source record present in the campaign checkout.
The identity decision relies on the separately evidenced native declaration rules. Active is the registry record state and confers no requirements on any TOML consumer.
